head: 8dcdfab
target: Repos opt into the push gate with a tracked, inert .own-your-diff marker that every clone inherits through git, plus a per-clone .git/hooks/pre-push hook the tool writes (install once, sync in every session), replacing git config core.hooksPath=.githooks.
incidental: selftest moved verbatim from skills/own-your-diff/scripts/ to top-level scripts/
SKILL.md: tool list rewritten for install/sync, selftest line dropped
agent-mode.md: examiners spawn fresh with none of the session's context
quizgate usage text for install and sync

questions.prompt: The old install ran `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Why does the design replace that with a tracked .own-your-diff marker plus a hook the tool writes locally?

options.label: Git refuses to run hooks that live inside the tracked tree, so the gate needed a separate opt-in channel

core.hooksPath is per-clone local config, so every clone needed a manual install and the repo had to ship a hooks directory; a tracked marker reaches every clone through git itself, and the tool adds the hook where it runs
A tracked marker lets CI run the quiz on every commit, which a local config value could not express
The marker's text tells quizgate how strictly to gate this repo, and core.hooksPath could not carry that setting

key_points: the opt-in must reach every clone, and the tracked tree is the only channel git shares; core.hooksPath was per-clone config set by hand in each clone
the marker is an inert presence signal: nothing ever reads its content, so it carries no settings
the old way also put the burden on the repo to carry a .githooks directory

questions.prompt: The marker is tracked; the hook is not. What does keeping hook code out of the tracked tree protect?

options.label: Hooks must differ from machine to machine, and tracked files are identical in every clone
The hook embeds each clone's absolute paths, which would collide if the hook were tracked
Selective gating: with the hook untracked, the repo can gate some clones and leave others free

Git executes nothing from the tree without per-clone wiring, so a tracked hook would be inert text until each clone wired it up anyway; writing .git/hooks/pre-push adds one hook where git already looks, instead of redirecting the clone's whole hooks path

key_points: git runs hooks only from the clone's hooks dir or a per-clone hooksPath, so a tracked hook script would be dead text until every clone wired it up by hand, the manual step the marker exists to remove
writing .git/hooks/pre-push installs exactly one hook where git already looks, rather than hijacking the clone's entire hooks path
the tree can carry the marker safely precisely because it is inert; executable behavior is materialized only on machines where the tool runs

questions.prompt: A clone has our hook installed, but quizgate is on neither PATH nor ~/.local/bin — the user removed it. What happens when they push, and why is that the right behavior for a gate?

options.label: The push is blocked with a message pointing at installing the tool: where the gate exists, it fails closed, because a gate that cannot run may not let pushes slip through silently
The push goes through; a gate that cannot run cannot block anything
The push goes through, but the hook records the unquizzed commits in the ledger for next time
The hook reinstalls quizgate from the plugin directory and then runs the check

key_points: fail-closed: the hook exits nonzero when it cannot run the gate, so the push is blocked
the block is actionable: it tells the author what to install, not just that something is missing
fail-open belongs only to clones where the tool never wrote a hook; once the hook exists, losing the tool must not reopen the gate

questions.prompt: Which of these leave a push from an opted-in repo completely ungated — no quiz, no block? Pick all that apply.

options.label: A fresh clone on a machine where the plugin has never run
A clone whose own pre-push hook never gained the gate line, because write_hook refused to touch it
A clone with our installed hook where quizgate is gone from PATH and from ~/.local/bin
A clone that already has our hook when the marker is later deleted from the repo

key_points: no hook, no gate: in clones where sync never ran, the marker is inert and pushes go through
a foreign hook left without the gate line leaves that clone ungated rather than blocked; the refusal costs coverage, never correctness
an installed hook gates with no regard for the marker: deleting the marker stops future installs only
losing quizgate under an installed hook blocks the push: fail-closed, not ungated

questions.prompt: The repo opts in with `quizgate install`. A teammate's clone already has a pre-push hook they wrote themselves — a secret scanner. Walk their clone through the design: what does the tool do there, what must the teammate do, and what would be lost if write_hook instead appended the gate line to any hook it found?
key_points: write_hook sees a hook it did not write, refuses to touch it, and prints the one line to add (quizgate check || exit 1): the human owns the merge, because the tool cannot safely edit hook code it does not understand
once the teammate adds the line, scanner and gate run in the same hook; until then their pushes stay ungated — the refusal trades coverage for ownership
silently appending would blur who owns the hook and could break it (ordering, exit status, an exec line); the tag grep keeps only the tool's own installs idempotent
